item.title: Paraguay's former president charged after bank collapse
item.description:
Santiago Peña was detained minutes after he was impeached by Congress, as protesters took to the streets demanding answers after the suspension of the Ueno bank Paraguay’s rightwing president has been placed under house arrest minutes after he was impeached by Congress, amid a severe crisis that left more than half the country’s population unable to access their bank accounts. Santiago Peña is being investigated about allegations he used his political influence to favour a bank that expanded exponentially under his government and was suspended this week after irregularities . item.title: Kenyan cult leader sentenced to 200 years in prison
item.description:
A Kenyan doomsday cult leader was sentenced Friday to 200 years in prison for the murders of 191 people after ordering followers to starve themselves to meet Jesus. Pastor Paul Mackenzie was sentenced by Kenya’s High Court in the coastal city of Mombasa after being convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult, according to the Associated Press. He received two consecutive 100-year terms: one for murders by starvation and another for murders by direct homicide. Justice Diana Kavedza said Mackenzie, the leader of the Good News International Church, bore the “primary criminal culpability” for leading his followers into an isolated area and directing them to starve themselves to death, the outlet reported. “The sentence is appropriate and just, to send an unmistakable message that such atrocities warrant the maximum penalties allowed by law,” the judge added. item.title: New Zealand faces weeks of uncertainty with election ‘too close to call’
item.description:
National party will be largest in parliament but ultimate shape of next government won’t be settled for some time New Zealand could be facing a weeks-long wait to know the shape of its next government, after its nail-biting election failed to hand a decisive victory to either the incumbent rightwing coalition or opposition left bloc. On preliminary results, the centre-right National party, led by the prime minister, Christopher Luxon, managed to secure enough seats to govern alongside its traditional coalition partners, the libertarian Act and populist New Zealand First parties. item.title: Texas’ School Voucher Program Could Be “Unrecognizable, If Not Extinct,” Says Democratic Lawmaker
item.description:
Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa at a rally in Austin on Election Day. Leila Saidane for The Texas Tribune Texas Gov. Greg Abbott’s vision for education was finally coming together. This year, the state launched a voucher program that allowed roughly 110,000 of Texas’ more than 5 million schoolchildren to get a private education using taxpayer dollars. Abbott’s loyal appointee at the Texas Education Agency, Commissioner Mike Morath, was leading the state’s largest takeover of public schools in recent history . And the Texas State Board of Education, with Abbott’s support , helped pass a controversial new social studies curriculum that required teaching Bible stories and shifted away from world history to focus on Texas and the United States. item.title: FAA announces first US digital air traffic control towers in Florida and Alaska
item.description:
Systems provide 360-degree view of airport operations, but concerns have been raised about the technology The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has announced that the first digital air traffic control towers in the US are officially operational, bringing new technology first to smaller airports in Florida and Alaska as the Trump administration presses ahead with updating the country’s ageing aviation infrastructure. The systems are now online at the Bartow executive airport (KBOW) in Florida and the Kenai municipal airport (PAEN) in Alaska, with five additional regional airports slated to receive the technology next. item.title: France sees new round of Yellow Vest, student protests
item.description:
French unions and student groups are set to take to the streets for another day of protests on Saturday, while the Yellow Vests movement plans a separate rally in central Paris despite a ban by authorities. The demonstrations follow weeks of youth-led unrest and nationwide strikes that drew hundreds of thousands of workers protesting over the rising cost of living. Paul Smith, Associate Professor in French history and politics at the University of Nottingham, and James André, France 24 reporter at Place de la République, share further insights.

Sources: Deutsche Welle, France 24
